scientific.integrity: The foundational fractional-illumination paper and the closest full Platonic-solid illumination paper were materially inspected. The new incidence and covering assertions are independently certified by exact arithmetic over Q(sqrt(5)) and exhaustive finite enumeration; no random search or timeout is used in the proof.
limitations: The ordinary icosahedral illumination value is prior-covered and is used only as a consistency benchmark, not as new content.
The vertex-transitive symmetry identity reduces fractional illumination to a one-direction incidence maximum but does not by itself compute that maximum for arbitrary vertex-transitive polytopes.
The finite certificates use the regular Euclidean realizations and do not extend automatically to nonregular polytopes with the same face lattice.
The 2012 Platonic-solid paper supplies closely related illumination geometry, so a short-corollary historical overlap risk remains.

title: Exact fractional illumination of the regular dodecahedron and icosahedron
